Check a JSON input file against a TreePPL model

Source: R/data.R
tp_input_check.Rd

Compares the top-level fields of a JSON input file with the arguments of the model function in a .tppl file, and reports the result in the console. Use it before running a model to catch misspelled, missing or extra inputs.

Usage

tp_input_check(json, tppl)

Arguments

json

Path to a JSON input file, e.g. one written by tp_write_tppl_json().

tppl

Path to the .tppl model file.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class tpIcheck with elements:

  • json_file, model_file: the paths given in json and tppl.

  • model_name: the file name of tppl without .tppl.

  • valid: TRUE if the JSON fields and the model arguments match exactly, FALSE otherwise.

  • missing: model arguments that are not in the JSON file.

  • extra: JSON fields that the model does not take.

  • expect_args: all model arguments, in signature order.

  • fields: all top-level JSON fields.

Details

The check covers names only: it does not test whether each value has the right type. See tp_expected_input() for the R object each argument expects.

See also

print.tpIcheck() for the console output, tp_expected_input(), tp_write_tppl_json().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tp_input_check(
  json = "json/testdata_qt.json",
  tppl = "models/pheno-mol/qt.tppl"
)

# Stop a script if the input does not match the model
if (!tp_input_check("input.json", "qt.tppl")$valid) {
  stop("Fix the input file first.")
}
} # }
